actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The MJCF root element declares the model humanoid-legged-description and uses radians.
The model option sets timestep 0.001 s, 50 iterations, the PGS solver, gravity 0 0 -9.81 and noslip_iterations 20.
The base_link body carries a freejoint.

The left leg is a chain of six hinge joints from leg_l1_joint to leg_l6_joint, and the right leg is a chain of six hinge joints from leg_r1_joint to leg_r6_joint; each joint declares its own range and actuatorfrcrange.
The actuator section declares twelve motor actuators, one per leg hinge, each with ctrllimited true and a ctrlrange of -150 to 150, -200 to 200 or -90 to 90 depending on the joint.
The model provides a keyframe named home whose qpos is 0 0 1.5, the identity quaternion and twelve zero joint angles.
mujoco_base.MuJoCoBase.__init__ loads the XML path with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path and creates an MjData.
The module function main of humanoid_sim initialises rclpy, resolves the installed humanoid_legged_description share path to mjcf/humanoid_legged_control_.xml and constructs HumanoidSim with it.
init_base_pos is 0 0 0.82 and init_joint_pos is twelve joint values, both defined at module scope.
After super().__init__ loads the model, HumanoidSim.__init__ sets qpos[:3] to init_base_pos, qpos[3:7] to a scipy quaternion of init_base_eular_zyx and the last twelve qpos values to init_joint_pos.
HumanoidSim computes data.ctrl as targetTorque plus Kp and Kd errors against targetPos, targetVel and the last twelve qpos/qvel values, then calls mj.mj_step.
HumanoidSim's node publishes /jointsPosVel, /ground_truth/state, /imu, /realTorque and /pauseFlag and subscribes to /targetTorque, /targetPos, /targetVel, /targetKp and /targetKd.
HumanoidSim sets simend to 1000.0 s and sim_rate to 1000.0 Hz.

The simulation loop runs until the GLFW window close flag; each outer pass runs inner iterations while no more than 1/60 s of simulated time has passed since the pass began and the pause flag is clear, and calls mj_step only when the wall clock has advanced by 1 / sim_rate.

determinism.notes: The stand-in is deterministic but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics; a reset seed is accepted and unused.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the MJCF for the free base, the twelve hinge joints, the twelve motor actuators, their explicit ctrlranges and the 0.001 s option step, then gives each actuated hinge a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value and holds the free base where the model puts it; it computes no inertia, torque, gravity, contact, friction, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory
the stand-in loads no STL mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact; the floor, obstacle boxes, joint ranges and armature attributes of the model are not applied

the upstream HumanoidSim overrides the model start state (qpos 0 0 0.82, a scipy quaternion and twelve init joint angles) and computes data.ctrl from targetTorque/targetPos/targetVel with its own Kp/Kd vectors; this driver calls mj_resetData, which restores the model defaults and does not apply the home keyframe, and takes the control vector from the caller

the upstream loop is wall-clock paced (about 1/60 s of simulated time per outer iteration, engine steps at 1/1000 s) and needs a GLFW window; this driver is lockstep with no wall-clock pacing and no GUI
the ROS 2 target and state topics, the /pauseFlag publication and the controller nodes are not used: the driver serves only the MuJoCo world step and reset, and no ROS graph was contacted
no physical humanoid is modelled and nothing was validated against the humanoid hardware

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
